subject: kukri snake
title: This Snake Doesn't Swallow Toads. It Cuts Them Open Instead

scenes.text: This snake doesn't swallow its prey. It opens it.
In Thailand, the small-banded kukri snake hunts a toad that carries a potent toxin in glands on its neck and back.
So it doesn't swallow. Its back teeth curve like tiny knives, and it uses them to slice the toad's belly.
Then it pushes its whole head inside and eats the organs, one at a time.
One struggle lasted nearly three hours. Scientists think the snake is dodging the poison.
No snake had ever been seen feeding this way until 2020. And yes, it's harmless to people.

description:
The small-banded kukri snake of Thailand doesn't swallow large toads. It cuts them open.
Its enlarged rear teeth, shaped like the curved kukri knife, slice the belly of the Asian black-spotted toad, and the snake puts its head inside to eat the organs one by one. Researchers reported three such attacks in the journal Herpetozoa in 2020, one lasting nearly three hours, and think the snake may be avoiding the toxin in the toad's neck and back glands. A smaller toad was swallowed whole.
What's the strangest way you've heard of a predator eating?
first_comment: In a fourth case the snake swallowed a young toad whole, so smaller toads may be less toxic. Which predator has the strangest table manners?
